en: Half cup oats (50 g)
Half onion and 1 carrot, chopped
1 small tomato
1 tsp oil
Turmeric, cumin, mustard seeds, salt
Dry-toast the oats in a pan for 2 minutes
Heat the oil, add mustard and cumin seeds
Add the vegetables and spices, stir 3 minutes
Add the oats and a cup of water, cook until absorbed
60 g split moong dal, soaked
1 garlic clove and a piece of ginger
Half onion and 1 green chilli, chopped
1 tsp oil
Turmeric, fresh coriander, salt
Blend the soaked dal with garlic, ginger and a little water
Stir the onion, chilli and spices into the batter
Pour a ladle onto a hot pan and spread it thin
Cook 2 minutes per side until golden

name.en: Poha (Flattened Rice with Onion and Peanuts)

en: Flattened rice (poha) 60 g
1 medium onion, chopped
1 small boiled potato, diced, 50 g
Peanuts 10 g
1 tsp oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves
Turmeric, salt, lemon juice and fresh coriander
Rinse the poha briefly in a sieve under cold water and let it rest 5 minutes until soft but not mushy.
Heat the oil and toast the mustard seeds, peanuts and curry leaves, then add the onion until translucent.
Add the potato, turmeric and salt and stir for two minutes.
Fold in the poha and toss gently over low heat for 3 minutes, then finish with lemon juice and coriander.
Fermented dosa batter 150 g
1 small onion, finely chopped
Half a green bell pepper, chopped
1 small tomato, chopped
1 tsp oil
Salt, fresh coriander and green chilli
Stir the batter gently and season it with salt.
Heat a non-stick griddle, brush it with half the oil and pour the batter into a thick circle.
Scatter the onion, pepper, tomato and coriander over the surface, press them in lightly and cook 3-4 minutes on medium heat.
Flip and cook 2 minutes until the vegetables soften and the base is golden, then serve with chutney.
Fermented idli batter 120 g
Dried toor dal 25 g
Mixed vegetables (carrot, aubergine, okra) 60 g
1 tsp oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves
1 tsp tamarind paste and sambar powder
Turmeric, salt and fresh coriander
Pour the idli batter into greased moulds and steam 10-12 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean.
Boil the dal with turmeric until completely soft, then mash it.
Cook the vegetables in a little water until tender, add the dal, tamarind paste and sambar powder and simmer 5 minutes.
Heat the oil with the mustard seeds and curry leaves, pour it into the sambar and serve hot with the idli.
Coarse semolina 50 g
Chopped vegetables (carrot, peas, pepper) 60 g
1 small onion, chopped, and grated ginger
2 tsp oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves
Cashews or peanuts 8 g
Salt, 150 ml water, lemon juice and coriander
Toast the semolina in a dry pan over low heat for 3-4 minutes until fragrant but not coloured, then set it aside.
Heat the oil and toast the mustard seeds, cashews and curry leaves, then add the onion and ginger until softened.
Add the vegetables, salt and water and bring to a boil.
Rain in the semolina while stirring constantly until the water is absorbed, cover for two minutes, then finish with lemon juice and coriander.
Fermented dosa batter 150 g
Boiled potato, coarsely mashed, 100 g
1 small onion, chopped
1 tsp oil, mustard seeds and curry leaves
Turmeric, chopped green chilli and salt
Lemon juice and fresh coriander
Heat the oil and toast the mustard seeds and curry leaves, then add the onion and green chilli until softened.
Add the turmeric, mashed potato and salt and stir for 3-4 minutes, then finish with lemon juice and coriander and set aside.
Heat a non-stick griddle and pour the batter into a very thin circle, drizzling a little oil around the edges.
Once the base is done, spoon the filling into the centre and fold the dosa over it, then serve immediately.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g
Fresh fenugreek leaves, chopped, 30 g
Low-fat yogurt 80 g (half in the dough, half for serving)
1 tsp oil
Turmeric, red chilli, cumin and salt
Water as needed
Knead the flour with the fenugreek, a quarter of the yogurt, the spices and salt, adding water gradually until you get a soft dough.
Rest it 10 minutes, then divide into balls and roll them thin.
Cook each disc on a hot griddle, brushing lightly with oil on both sides until golden spots appear.
Serve warm with the remaining yogurt.
Soaked tapioca pearls (sabudana) 50 g
Roasted, coarsely ground peanuts 15 g
Small potato, cubed, 50 g
1 tsp ghee or oil and cumin seeds
Chopped green chilli and grated ginger
Salt, lemon juice and fresh coriander
Soak the sabudana 4-6 hours or overnight until soft and the pearls separate, then drain any excess water.
Heat the ghee and toast the cumin, then add the potato and cook covered 5-6 minutes until tender.
Add the green chilli, ginger and peanuts and stir for a minute.
Add the sabudana and salt and stir gently over medium heat 5 minutes until translucent, then finish with lemon juice and coriander.
Broken wheat (daliya) 40 g
Chopped vegetables (carrot, peas, beans) 70 g
1 small onion, chopped
1 tsp ghee or oil and cumin seeds
Turmeric, salt and 300 ml water
Fresh coriander
Toast the broken wheat in a dry pan over low heat for 3 minutes until fragrant, then set aside.
Heat the ghee and toast the cumin, then add the onion until softened.
Add the vegetables and turmeric and stir for two minutes, then add the water and salt and bring to a boil.
Add the daliya, lower the heat and cook covered 15-18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and thick, then garnish with coriander.

serving.en: One plate (1 cup beans + 100 g rice)

en: 1 cup cooked kidney beans
100 g cooked basmati rice
1 onion and 2 tomatoes, puréed
1 tsp oil
Ginger, garlic, cumin, garam masala
Heat the oil, toast the cumin, then ginger and garlic
Add the onion-tomato purée and cook until the oil separates
Add the beans and a cup of water, simmer 10 minutes
Mash a few beans to thicken, serve over the rice
150 g chicken breast, cubed
3 tbsp low-fat yogurt
1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
Paprika, cumin, coriander, garam masala
Cucumber, tomato, onion, lemon
Mix the yogurt with the spices and ginger-garlic paste
Marinate the chicken and chill at least 30 minutes
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, turning once
Chop the vegetables, serve alongside with lemon
Basmati rice 180 g, cooked to 70 percent
Mixed vegetables (carrot, peas, beans, cauliflower) 120 g
Yogurt 40 g and fried onion 15 g
1 tbsp ghee or oil
Garlic-ginger paste, biryani masala, turmeric and salt
Mint, coriander and saffron strands in 2 tbsp milk
Boil the rice to 70 percent doneness with cardamom and bay leaf, then drain it.
Sauté the vegetables in the ghee with the garlic-ginger paste and spices for 5 minutes, then add the yogurt and cook until the sauce clings.
Layer the rice over the vegetables and scatter the fried onion, mint, coriander and saffron milk on top.
Seal the pot tightly and cook on very low heat 15 minutes, then fold gently before serving.
1 large aubergine 300 g
2 whole-wheat roti (80 g)
1 medium onion, chopped
1 medium tomato, chopped, and 2 crushed garlic cloves
1 tbsp oil
Cumin, turmeric, green chilli, salt and fresh coriander
Roast the aubergine directly over a flame or in the oven until the skin chars and the flesh is soft, then peel and mash it.
Heat the oil and brown the onion, then add the garlic, green chilli and cumin.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook until soft, then stir in the mashed aubergine and salt and cook 7 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve with the hot roti.
2 boiled eggs
Cooked basmati rice 120 g
1 medium onion, grated, and puréed tomato 100 g
2 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala
Salt and fresh coriander
Boil the eggs for ten minutes, peel them and score them shallowly so they soak up the sauce.
Brown the onion in the oil, then add the garlic-ginger paste and dry spices and stir for a minute.
Add the tomato and salt and cook until the oil separates, then pour in half a cup of water.
Slide the eggs into the sauce, simmer 5 minutes and serve over the rice with coriander.
Lean lamb 150 g, cubed
Cooked basmati rice 120 g
Yogurt 40 g
1 tbsp oil
Kashmiri red chilli, ground fennel, dried ginger, cardamom and cinnamon
1 grated onion and salt
Marinate the lamb in the yogurt with half the spices for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil and toast the cardamom and cinnamon, then add the onion and brown it.
Add the lamb with its marinade and stir until the colour changes, then add the remaining spices, salt and a cup of water.
Cover and cook on low heat 45-50 minutes until the meat is tender and the sauce thickens, then serve with the rice.

name.en: Malai Kofta in Cashew Sauce with Rice

en: Kofta shaped from mashed potato, grated carrot and a little chickpea flour, 120 g
Cooked basmati rice 120 g
Soaked and ground cashews 20 g
Puréed tomato 100 g and 1 medium onion
2 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, garam masala, turmeric, salt and light cream 20 g
Shape the potato, carrot and chickpea flour mixture into small balls and bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until firm and golden.
Brown the onion in the oil, add the garlic-ginger paste and spices, then the tomato and cook 7 minutes.
Add the ground cashews and half a cup of water and cook 5 minutes until the sauce is smooth, then stir in the cream.
Slip the kofta into the sauce two minutes before serving so they don't break apart, and serve over the rice.
Chicken breast, sliced, 130 g
1 whole-wheat roti (45 g)
Yogurt 30 g
Garlic-ginger paste, turmeric, red chilli and garam masala
Sliced onion, cucumber and tomato
Mint chutney, lemon juice and 1 tsp oil
Marinate the chicken in the yogurt, garlic, ginger, spices and salt for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pan and cook the chicken 6-8 minutes until fully done and browned at the edges.
Warm the roti on a dry griddle on both sides until pliable.
Spread the roti with mint chutney, add the chicken and vegetables and a squeeze of lemon, then roll it tightly.
Mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, potato, peas) 150 g
Cooked basmati rice 130 g
Soaked and ground cashews 20 g
Yogurt 40 g and 1 medium onion
2 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, turmeric, garam masala, cinnamon and cardamom
Parboil the vegetables until nearly tender and reserve the cooking water.
Brown the onion in the oil, add the garlic-ginger paste, cinnamon and cardamom and stir for a minute.
Add the turmeric and yogurt and stir briskly over low heat so it doesn't curdle.
Add the vegetables, reserved water, ground cashews and garam masala, and cook 10 minutes until the sauce thickens, then serve over the rice.
Fresh okra 200 g, sliced
2 whole-wheat roti (80 g)
1 medium onion and 1 medium tomato, sliced
1 tbsp oil
Cumin, turmeric, ground coriander, red chilli and amchur (dried mango powder) or lemon juice
Salt and fresh coriander
Dry the okra thoroughly after washing to reduce sliminess, and stir it in a dry pan for two minutes to drive off moisture.
Heat the oil and toast the cumin, then add the onion until golden.
Add the turmeric, ground coriander, red chilli and tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Add the okra and salt and stir gently over medium heat, uncovered, for 10-12 minutes until tender and less slimy, add the amchur and coriander, and serve with the roti.
100 g low-fat paneer, cubed
200 g fresh spinach
1 small onion, garlic, ginger
1 tsp oil
Cumin, garam masala, salt
Blanch the spinach 2 minutes, then blend smooth
Sauté the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil
Add the spinach purée and spices, cook 5 minutes
Fold in the paneer cubes, warm 2 minutes and serve
1 cup cooked chickpeas
1 onion and 2 tomatoes, chopped
Ginger-garlic paste
1 tbsp oil
Cumin, coriander, turmeric, amchur, garam masala
Toast the cumin in the oil, then brown the onion
Add the ginger-garlic paste, tomatoes and spices
Cook until the masala thickens and the oil separates
Add the chickpeas and half a cup of water, simmer 10 minutes
Skinless chicken thighs 150 g
Fresh grated coconut 20 g
1 medium onion and 1 medium tomato, chopped
1 tbsp oil
1 tsp coarse black pepper, 1 tsp ground coriander and 1 tsp fennel seeds
Curry leaves, garlic-ginger paste and salt
Toast the coconut with the black pepper, coriander and fennel over low heat until fragrant, then grind to a paste with a little water.
Heat the oil with the curry leaves and brown the onion, then add the garlic-ginger paste.
Add the chicken and sear it 5 minutes, then add the tomato and salt and cook until softened.
Stir in the ground paste and half a cup of water, cover and cook 15 minutes until the chicken is done and the sauce thickens.

name.en: Kerala Fish Moilee (Coconut Milk Fish Curry)

en: White fish fillets 150 g
Coconut milk 80 ml
1 medium onion sliced, 3 garlic cloves and grated ginger
2 tsp coconut oil
Turmeric, slit green chilli and curry leaves
Sliced tomato, salt and lemon juice
Season the fish with turmeric and salt and let it sit 10 minutes.
Heat the coconut oil with the curry leaves and soften the onion, garlic, ginger and green chilli without browning them.
Pour in the coconut milk with a pinch of turmeric and warm it gently without letting it boil.
Slide in the fish and tomato slices, cover and cook 8 minutes, then add the lemon juice and serve with rice.
Potato 100 g, cubed
Cauliflower 150 g, in florets
1 small onion and 1 small tomato, chopped
1 tbsp oil
Cumin, turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala
Grated ginger, green chilli, salt and fresh coriander
Heat the oil and toast the cumin, then add the onion, ginger and green chilli until softened.
Add the potato, turmeric and salt and cook covered for 5 minutes, stirring once.
Add the cauliflower, tomato and remaining spices, cover and cook 10-12 minutes, turning gently so the florets stay whole.
Uncover and stir for two minutes to dry off the moisture, then garnish with fresh coriander.
Low-fat paneer 120 g, cubed
Strained yogurt 40 g
Bell pepper and onion 80 g, in large pieces
1 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, red chilli, ground coriander and garam masala
Lemon juice, salt and chaat masala to finish
Whisk the yogurt with the garlic-ginger paste, spices, lemon juice and salt.
Coat the paneer cubes and vegetables in the marinade and chill them 30 minutes.
Thread them onto skewers and grill in a 220°C oven or on a griddle pan 12-15 minutes, turning until the edges char.
Brush with the oil in the last two minutes and finish with chaat masala and lemon juice before serving.
Cooked black lentils (urad dal) 150 g
Cooked red kidney beans, a couple of spoonfuls, 30 g
Puréed tomato 100 g and 1 medium onion, chopped
1 tsp butter and 1 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, cumin, turmeric and garam masala
Salt, light cream 15 g and fresh coriander
Melt the butter with the oil and brown the onion, then add the garlic-ginger paste, cumin and turmeric.
Add the tomato and cook until the oil separates from the sauce.
Add the lentils, beans and a cup of water and simmer 15-20 minutes, mashing a little to thicken the texture.
Stir in the garam masala, salt and cream, and serve hot garnished with coriander.
Potato 150 g, cubed
Peas 80 g (fresh or frozen)
Puréed tomato 80 g and 1 small onion
1 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, cumin, turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala
Salt and fresh coriander
Heat the oil and toast the cumin, then add the onion until golden.
Add the garlic-ginger paste, turmeric and ground coriander and stir for a minute.
Add the tomato and cook until softened, then add the potato, salt and a cup of water, cover and cook 12 minutes.
Add the peas and garam masala and cook 5 minutes more, then garnish with fresh coriander.
Firm white fish fillet (such as sea bass) 180 g
Strained yogurt 40 g
Garlic-ginger paste
Kashmiri red chilli, turmeric, ground cumin and garam masala
Lemon juice and salt
1 tsp oil for grilling
Mix the yogurt with the garlic-ginger paste, spices, lemon juice and salt.
Coat the fish slices in the marinade and chill 30 minutes.
Heat the grill or a griddle pan and brush it with oil.
Grill the fish 4-5 minutes per side until fully cooked with light char marks, and serve with lemon wedges.
Fresh white mushrooms 200 g, sliced
1 medium onion and 1 medium tomato, chopped
1 tsp oil
Garlic-ginger paste, cumin, turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala
Salt and fresh coriander
Chopped green chilli (optional)
Heat the oil and toast the cumin, then add the onion until golden.
Add the garlic-ginger paste, green chilli, turmeric and ground coriander and stir for a minute.
Add the tomato and cook until softened and the oil separates.
Add the mushrooms and salt and cook over medium heat 7-8 minutes until they release their water and it reduces slightly, add the garam masala and coriander and serve.
30 g makhana (fox nuts)
Half tsp oil or ghee
A pinch of turmeric
A pinch of black pepper
Salt
Heat the oil in a pan over low heat
Add the makhana and stir 6-8 minutes until crisp
Add turmeric, pepper and salt, toss for a minute
Cool completely before storing so they stay crunchy
1 cup moong sprouts
1 tomato and 1 small onion, chopped
Half a cucumber, chopped
Juice of half a lemon
Chaat masala, salt, fresh coriander
Steam the sprouts 2 minutes, or use them raw
Toss with the tomato, onion and cucumber
Add the lemon juice, chaat masala and salt
Top with coriander and serve straight away
Chickpea flour 50 g and 1 tbsp fine semolina
Low-fat yogurt 40 g and 60 ml water
1 tsp sugar, salt and lemon juice
Half a tsp baking soda
1 tsp oil, mustard seeds and sesame seeds
Curry leaves and fresh coriander
Mix the flour, semolina, yogurt, water, salt, sugar and lemon juice into a smooth batter.
Stir in the baking soda for ten seconds only, then pour the mixture into a greased tin.
Steam 12-15 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean, cool slightly and cut into squares.
Heat the oil with the mustard seeds, sesame and curry leaves, pour it over the pieces and garnish with coriander.
Puffed rice 20 g
Fried chickpea noodles (sev) 10 g and 1 crushed papdi cracker
Boiled potato, diced, 30 g
1 small onion and 1 small tomato, chopped
1 tbsp tamarind chutney and 1 tsp mint chutney
Lemon juice, chaat masala and fresh coriander
Toss the puffed rice with the potato, onion and tomato in a wide bowl.
Add both chutneys, the lemon juice and the chaat masala and mix quickly.
Fold in the sev, crushed papdi and coriander with a single stir.
Serve immediately so it stays crisp.
Chickpea flour 40 g
Sliced onion, chopped spinach and grated potato 80 g
1 tsp oil for the batter and 1 tsp for brushing
Cumin, turmeric, red chilli and carom seeds
Salt and a pinch of baking soda
About 30 ml water
Mix the vegetables with the flour, spices and salt and let them sit 5 minutes to release their moisture.
Add the water gradually until you have a thick batter that clings to the spoon, then stir in the baking soda and the teaspoon of oil.
Drop small spoonfuls onto a lined tray and brush them with the remaining oil.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes, turn them and bake 5-7 minutes more until crisp, then serve with chutney.
2 slices whole-wheat bread (60 g)
Boiled potato, sliced, 50 g
Cucumber, tomato and onion, sliced, 60 g
1 tbsp mint and coriander chutney
1 tsp butter
Chaat masala, salt and black pepper
Spread butter on one side of each slice and the mint chutney on the other.
Layer the potato slices, then the cucumber, tomato and onion, and sprinkle with chaat masala, salt and pepper.
Close the sandwich and press it in a toaster or a heavy pan for 4-5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Cut into triangles and serve immediately with the remaining chutney.
Soaked and ground urad lentils 40 g
A pinch of baking soda and salt
Low-fat yogurt 120 g
Tamarind chutney and mint chutney, 1 tsp each
Roasted ground cumin and red chilli
Fresh coriander
Whisk the ground lentils with the baking soda and salt until light and fluffy.
Drop small spoonfuls onto a hot non-stick pan and cook as small patties on both sides until done.
Soak them in warm water for 5 minutes, then squeeze gently.
Arrange on a plate, pour the yogurt over them, and add the chutneys, roasted cumin, red chilli and coriander.
Soaked and coarsely ground urad lentils 60 g
Finely chopped onion, green chilli and grated ginger
Chopped curry leaves and whole black pepper
Salt and a pinch of baking soda
1 tsp oil for brushing
Yogurt or chutney to serve
Whisk the ground lentils with the baking soda until light, then fold in the onion, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves, black pepper and salt.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into small discs with a hole in the centre.
Arrange them on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp, and serve with yogurt or chutney.
Boondi (fried chickpea flour pearls) 30 g
Low-fat yogurt 150 g
Roasted ground cumin and red chilli
Salt and a pinch of sugar
Fresh coriander
A pinch of black pepper (optional)
Soak the boondi in warm water for 5 minutes until soft, then squeeze gently.
Whisk the yogurt until smooth and add a pinch of salt and sugar.
Gently fold the boondi into the yogurt.
Sprinkle with roasted cumin, red chilli and coriander, and serve chilled.
Boiled or grilled corn kernels 150 g
1 small onion and 1 small tomato, chopped
1 tsp butter or oil
Chaat masala, red chilli and roasted ground cumin
Lemon juice and salt
Fresh coriander and chopped green chilli (optional)
Heat the butter in a pan, add the corn and stir for two minutes until warmed through.
Add the onion and tomato and stir for another minute.
Add the chaat masala, red chilli, roasted cumin and salt and mix.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander, and serve warm or chilled.
150 g strained (Greek) yogurt
1 tsp honey
A pinch of ground cardamom
A few saffron threads
Crushed pistachios or almonds
Soak the saffron in a spoon of warm milk for 5 minutes
Whisk the yogurt with the honey until smooth
Stir in the cardamom and the saffron
Chill 30 minutes and top with the nuts
10 pitted dates
3 tbsp desiccated coconut
1 tbsp crushed almonds
A pinch of ground cardamom
1 tsp ghee (optional)
Blitz the dates to a paste in a processor
Toast the coconut and almonds 2 minutes on low heat
Mix everything with the cardamom and ghee
Roll into small balls, coat in coconut and chill
Grated carrot 200 g
Full-fat milk 150 ml
Sugar 15 g
1 tsp ghee
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
Chopped almonds and pistachios 8 g
Heat the ghee and stir the grated carrot for 5 minutes until fragrant and no longer raw.
Pour in the milk and cook over medium heat, stirring, until the carrot absorbs it completely (20-25 minutes).
Add the sugar and cardamom and keep stirring until the mixture dries out and turns glossy.
Stir in the nuts and serve warm or chilled.

name.en: Bengali Sandesh (Fresh Cheese Sweet with Cardamom)

en: Fresh milk 400 ml
1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar
Icing sugar 15 g
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
Chopped pistachios 5 g
Saffron strands (optional)
Bring the milk to a boil, turn off the heat and add the lemon juice gradually until the curds separate from the whey.
Strain the curds in a muslin cloth, rinse them under cold water and squeeze out the moisture thoroughly.
Knead the cheese with the heel of your hand on a smooth surface for 5 minutes until silky, then work in the sugar and cardamom.
Warm it in a non-stick pan over low heat 3-4 minutes until it holds together, shape into discs, top with pistachios and chill.
Full-fat milk 200 ml
Sugar 12 g
Ground pistachios 8 g
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
A few saffron strands
1 tsp cornflour dissolved in water
Simmer the milk over low heat, stirring, until it reduces by about half and thickens (25-30 minutes).
Add the dissolved cornflour, sugar, cardamom, saffron and two thirds of the pistachios and cook 2 minutes.
Cool the mixture completely, then pour it into kulfi moulds or small cups.
Freeze at least 6 hours, dip the mould in warm water to release it and top with the remaining pistachios.
Rice flour 30 g
60 ml water, a pinch of salt and a drop of oil
Fresh grated coconut 25 g
Jaggery 15 g
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
A pinch of nutmeg
Warm the coconut with the jaggery over low heat 4-5 minutes until the sugar melts and the filling holds together, then add the cardamom and nutmeg and let it cool.
Boil the water with the salt and the drop of oil, add the rice flour all at once, stir quickly and cover for 3 minutes.
Knead the dough while still warm until smooth, shape small discs, place the filling in the centre and gather the edges into a peak.
Steam 10 minutes over a damp cloth and serve warm.
Fresh strained cheese (paneer) 100 g
1 tsp fine semolina
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Sugar 15 g
A quarter tsp ground cardamom and saffron strands
Chopped pistachios 5 g
Knead the cheese with the semolina using the heel of your hand for 5 minutes until smooth like dough, then shape into small flat discs.
Boil them in water with a little sugar for 10-12 minutes until they double in size and float, then squeeze gently.
Warm the milk with the sugar, cardamom and saffron over low heat until it reduces by a third and thickens slightly.
Place the discs in the milk and let them soak for 10 minutes, chill for an hour, and garnish with pistachios.
Chickpea flour (besan) 50 g
2 tsp ghee
Icing sugar 15 g
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
Chopped pistachios or almonds 5 g
A pinch of nutmeg (optional)
Heat the ghee in a heavy pan over low heat, add the chickpea flour and stir constantly for 10-12 minutes until it turns golden and smells toasted.
Remove from the heat, add the cardamom and nutmeg and stir to cool slightly.
Once just warm, add the icing sugar and mix well.
Shape into small balls between your palms while still warm, top with the nuts, and let them firm up fully before serving.

name.en: Anjeer Barfi (Dried Fig and Nut Fudge)

en: Dried figs, stems removed, 60 g
Chopped almonds, walnuts and pistachios 25 g
1 tsp ghee
A quarter tsp ground cardamom
1 tsp warm water to soften the figs
A pinch of nutmeg (optional)
Soak the dried figs in warm water for 10 minutes until soft, then blend them in a food processor into a firm paste.
Heat the ghee in a pan, add the fig paste and cardamom and stir over low heat 4-5 minutes until it comes together.
Add two thirds of the nuts and stir, then spread the mixture on baking paper to an even thickness.
Sprinkle the remaining nuts and press gently, chill 30 minutes, and cut into squares.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g
1 tsp ghee for the dough and 1 tsp for brushing
Filling of dried milk solids (khoya) or milk powder 30 g
Almonds, desiccated coconut and chopped pistachios 15 g
Icing sugar 15 g and ground cardamom
Water as needed
Knead the flour with the ghee and a little water into a fairly firm dough, and let it rest covered for 20 minutes.
Mix the khoya with the nuts, icing sugar and cardamom into a firm filling.
Roll the dough into small thin discs, place the filling in the centre, fold into a half-moon and press the edges tightly to seal, or crimp with a fork.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush with ghee, then bake at 180°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
